verified.exploit_entry_point: The public library modules loaded with the project's own AMD loader (mout/object/deepMixIn, deepFillIn, set, namespace, unset, get, has), exactly as the project's own specs load them. The hidden cases call these modules directly and compute every expected value as a literal; no product code is used to compute expectations or to clean up.
sites: src/object/deepMixIn.js:15,23-27 (copyProp recurses into the inherited Object.prototype for an own __proto__ key)
src/object/deepFillIn.js:15-23 (the fill-only sibling reaches the same inherited object through its non-null branch)
src/object/set.js:7-12 (the regex coerces a non-string path while the guard, if any, sees the raw value)
src/object/namespace.js:8-14 (a segment resolved only on the prototype chain is followed into a shared prototype)
src/object/unset.js:7-14 (deletion walks through inherited segments onto Object.prototype)
src/object/get.js:8-16, src/object/has.js:8-10 (readers that must keep their inherited semantics)
routes: T1: deepFillIn with a top-level and with a nested own __proto__ key in the defaults
T2: deepMixIn with a top-level, a nested and a later-source own __proto__ key
T3: set with an inherited-name path, with a __proto__ first segment and with a non-string path; namespace with inherited-name and __proto__ segments
T4: unset with constructor.prototype and __proto__ paths that resolve onto Object.prototype

verified.project_tests_run: NODE_PATH=/opt/verifier/node_modules node tests/runner.js in the built image at the pinned commit: 1060 tests, 0 failures. The same command on the reference fix: 1060 tests, 0 failures.

traps.shape: the same own-key copy implemented a second time in the fill-only deep copy: a source that owns a __proto__ key makes the non-null branch recurse into the destination's inherited Object.prototype; coupled must-keep-working: missing own properties are filled, existing own children are recursed into, and non-plain values are copied by reference
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the fill-only loop assigns a key only when the current value is null or undefined, so a reader can argue the inherited __proto__ slot is already non-null and can never be filled; the advisory's own example uses the mixing sibling

security/deep-fill-in-nested-proto::deep fill of a nested __proto__ key does not reach Object.prototype

functional/deep-fill-in-reference-values::deep fill copies non-plain values by reference
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the fill-only twin is in the same family as the reported helper and is still unguarded at the latest upstream revision

traps.shape: the dotted-path writer family: the published fix guards the setter with a raw-value substring scan, but a path supplied in a non-string form is coerced by the writer after the scan; the setter's own lower-level namespace creator is public and unguarded, so a segment resolved only on the prototype chain is followed into a shared prototype; coupled must-keep-working: existing own child objects are reused, a plain nested write still creates missing children, and non-nested writes still work
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the setter and the namespace creator take a dotted path from the caller rather than from the untrusted object the report describes, and their documented job is just to create nested properties; a guard that rejects only the literal __proto__ spelling still leaves the inherited-name form working

security/set-proto-segment::a path whose first segment is __proto__ does not write a shared prototype
security/set-non-string-path::a dotted path supplied in a non-string form does not write a shared prototype
security/namespace-constructor-prototype::creating a namespace cannot follow an inherited constructor
security/namespace-proto-segment::creating a namespace cannot follow an inherited __proto__ segment
coupled_functional_tests: functional/set-and-namespace::nested property creation reuses own children and keeps ordinary keys
traps.realistic_because: published fix site: both fix commits change the setter, and its namespace dependency plus the non-string path form are still unguarded at the latest upstream revision

traps.shape: the dotted-path deleter: a path that resolves through the inherited constructor or __proto__ walks onto Object.prototype and deletes the named property there; the shared reader it uses must keep answering inherited names as present, so the guard cannot live in the reader; coupled must-keep-working: own nested and top-level deletes still work, a missing path still returns true, and has/get keep their inherited semantics
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the deleter writes no attacker-controlled value and only removes a property that already exists, and the readers are read-only, so this looks outside a pollution advisory; a blanket segment ban in the shared reader breaks the project's own requirement that inherited names read as present

security/unset-proto-segment::deleting a path cannot reach a shared prototype through __proto__

traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: still unguarded at the latest upstream revision

A.summary: Prototype pollution through the recursive object copy helpers (published as fixed in 1.2.3; the published commit guards the dotted-path setter, not the named copy helpers)

B.summary: Incomplete-fix bypass of the same guard: the path is coerced after the raw-value scan; the later commit stringifies the path first (published as fixed in 1.2.4)

history.pinned_rule: first parent of A's fix commit 3fecf133 (git log: parents 2189378 and 397fa13); package.json at HEAD is version 1.2.2 and no source file carries a dangerous-key guard

wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: this is a library, where a thrown error is an acceptable refusal and the security cases treat it as blocked; a crash that also breaks legitimate use is caught by the functional suite
wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: the bug is not resource-scoped; every helper acts on the destination the caller passes, so no neighbouring resource can be substituted
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: the library has no roles or request directions; the security cases cover copying, writing and deleting
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: no normalising or adjusting step runs between the caller's input and the sink
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: there is no authority or identity decision in this library
